title: Foreign adapter build graph invalidation
objective: Make ordinary builds regenerate and rebuild every generated foreign-library host adapter exactly when its declaration, generated source, or build inputs change, with focused stale-addon regression tests and no gratuitous warm rebuilds.

oracles: Generated adapter manifest content and filesystem mtimes across cold, warm, and changed-input builds

handoff.summary: Ordinary builds now regenerate deterministic FFI lowerings before module-cache construction, then reconcile every already-installed FLINT, FFLAS, igraph, and M4RI generated host adapter before production-kernel publication. The installed manifest records the complete native compiler cache key and addon hash, so declaration, wrapper-generator, compiler/backend, toolchain, target, foreign-header/library, or artifact-byte drift republishes exactly the stale adapter. Missing optional adapters are reported and remain unprovisioned; current warm adapters are not republished. Focused tests cover ordering, empty optional build directories, warm no-op operation, stale manifests, changed native cache identities, and tampered addons. Complete ordinary-build trials confirmed both FLINT-only stale repair and unchanged warm mtimes.
risks: Cross-platform behavior is mechanically covered by platform-neutral path and hashing logic, and the compiler cache already owns Windows/Darwin target identity, but the validation receipts in this worktree are linux-x64 only.

The broad changed-file runner reached an inherited standalone compiler fixture failure: compiler/matrix.py cannot import sagejs.linear_algebra.matrix_selection_public. This is pre-existing on the integration branch and outside this lane; build, architecture, portable, strict, and focused FFI validation passed.
next_steps: Run an independent review of commit 2ec5b0a before integration.
